newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal foreign minister resigns over local polls.
newsitem.headline: Nepal foreign minister resigns over local polls.

text.p: Nepal's Foreign Minister quit on Wednesday, accusing the ruling coalition's dominant communists of cheating in last month's local government elections.
Prakash Chandra Lohani told reporters he had resigned in protest against "widespread rigging and intimidation" by the United Marxist-Leninist party in the May 17 and 26 vote.
Lohani belongs to Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand's Rashtriya Prajatantra Party, which rules in uneasy alliance with the more powerful communists.
State television said King Birendra accepted Lohani's resignation and Chand asked Housing Minister Kamal Thapa to take responsibility for the Foreign Ministry.
Rajeswar Devkota, co-chairman of Chand's party, told Reuters the resignation was "unlikely to have adverse effect on the government". A regular session of parliament is due to begin on June 26.

Chand's party controls only 20 seats in the 205-member House of Representatives, the lower house of Nepal's parliament, while the Marxist-Leninists hold 90 seats. Nepal has had three coalition governments since the present parliament was elected in 1994.
At least six people died in violence during last month's local government voting, which elected nearly 190,000 representatives in 4,000 villages and 58 municipalities.
Latest results showed the Marxist-Leninist UML had won over 88,000 places and the royalist RPP only 21,000.
The main opposition Nepali Congress party which has won 50,000 places has also alleged widespread election fraud.
Officials have ordered re-polls in 437 places affected by violence, and full results are expected this week.

"This campaign of intimidation, threats and strong-arm tactics of the UML sustained by the help of the administration, found the RPP a silent spectator, helpless and without any defence," Lohani said in a statement.
He said he had told the prime minister that "the notion that the state machinery can be used to strengthen the party is a theme against democratic norms and values."

"I should have resigned even earlier than today but the Prime Minister of India was coming to Nepal and I was aware of the possibility of achieving progress in many areas of national interest during the visit," Lohani said.

Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, making a three-day visit last week, signed agreements on Nepali access to Bangladesh across Indian territory, water sharing and private trade in electric power.
Chand also brought three new junior ministers into his cabinet on Wednesday evening, state television said.
